sections.title: AI & ML
sections.body: Anthropic Adds Opt-In Security Scanning for Critical Open-Source Projects (InfoQ). Swedish government offices to ban ChatGPT and Claude (Hacker News). NgRx 22: Resource Extensions and Dynamic Deep Signals for Angular (InfoQ). 101 Best Financial Data APIs in 2026 (Dev.to Programming). 1Password launches a way for AI agents to log in on your behalf without seeing your password (TechCrunch AI).

digest.key_takeaway: AI company Anthropic has launched OSS Scanner, a free, opt-in service to find vulnerabilities in open-source projects. Enrolled maintainers receive periodic security reports generated by the company's strongest models, including Claude Mythos. The reports are sent without human review, and project maintainers can choose to validate their findings and decide which proposed fixes to accept. By Matt Saunders

articles.title: NgRx 22: Resource Extensions and Dynamic Deep Signals for Angular
articles.summary: NgRx 22 adds experimental resource extensions that change Angular's resource behavior, so value() is retained during reloads and no longer throws on errors. It also introduces dynamic deep signals for union types, a SignalStoreFeatureType utility, and ESLint v10 support. Upgrading requires Angular 22 and TypeScript 6.0, and most breaking changes have automated migrations. By Daniel Curtis

articles.title: OpenShell vs Docker Sandboxes: Which AI Agent Runtime Should You Choose?
articles.summary:
An AI coding agent can read a repository, run shell commands, install packages, and send network requests. That is useful until a tool call reaches the wrong file, leaks a token, or downloads code that behaves differently than expected.

Two projects now aim to put a boundary around that work: NVIDIA OpenShell and Docker Sandboxes. They solve related problems, but they are not interchangeable products. OpenShell is a policy-driven runtime and control plane for governing agent access across sandboxes. Docker Sandboxes is a developer-facing way to run coding agents in isolated local or cloud env

articles.title: Why AI Agents Need Idempotency Keys Before They Touch Your APIs
articles.summary:

articles.title: The Best Candidate Didn’t Reject Your Offer, Your Hiring Process Did
articles.summary:
Hiring the right talent is only half the challenge. A slow or confusing hiring process can cause even the most qualified candidates to walk away.

🚩 Common Hiring Mistakes

Lengthy interview rounds that delay decisions.

Poor communication that leaves candidates waiting for updates.

Slow approvals that allow competitors to move faster.

Unclear expectations that create doubts about the role.

💡 How Can Companies Improve?

✅ Streamline interviews and remove unnecessary steps.

✅ Prioritize timely feedback and transparent communication.

✅ Align hiring managers to enable faster decision-making.

articles.title: Xcode 27.2: What Developers Need to Know (Including the New JSON Project Format)
articles.summary:
Xcode 27.2 is a point release, but it ships one change that will affect almost every team sooner or later: a new JSON-based project file that replaces the old project.pbxproj. The rest of the release is a mix of small features, a solid batch of Device Hub and Previews fixes, and a few known issues you should know about before you upgrade your CI machines.

This post walks through what matters, in order of how likely it is to affect your day.

articles.title: Vercel Labs Open-Sources fx: A Zig Coding Agent Designed to Be Embedded
articles.summary: Vercel Labs has released fx, an experimental open-source coding agent written in Zig. It runs as a CLI, a script component, or an embedded library, including a WebAssembly build. Early feedback questioned its model-agnostic claim and a name conflict with an existing tool. Vercel says the project is pre-1.0 and changing quickly. By Daniel Curtis

articles.title: Harbor Adds Docker Sandboxes to Run Reproducible AI Agent Evals in Isolated MicroVMs
articles.summary: Docker announced that Harbor, the open-source agent evaluation framework, now works with Docker Sandboxes. This change allows each evaluation task to run in its own microVM. So, instead of sharing a container, tasks are isolated for better performance By Claudio Masolo
